Chief justice: Judges must not use AI to write verdicts
item.description:
Judges may use artificial intelligence (AI) to search for relevant information and legal references, but must not rely on it to prepare or write verdicts, Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury has said.
He stressed that the operative part of every verdict must be written personally by the concerned judge, based on their own judicial judgement, legal reasoning and analysis.
The chief justice made the remarks while addressing members of the Bangladesh Judicial Service working in courts and tribunals across Chittagong division at a program at Radisson Blu Bay View Hotel in Chittagong on Saturday.
Judicial officers from all 11 districts of the division — Chittagong, Comilla, Cox's Bazar, Noakhali, Brahmanbaria, Chandpur, Lakshmipur, Feni, Khagrachhari, Rangamati and Bandarban — attended the event.
He emphasised speeding up judicial proceedings, modernising case management, improving judicial efficiency and ensuring a court-friendly environment for litigants.
Highlighting the importance of social realities and a humane approach in judicial decisions, he said judges should consider the broader social context alongside the legal aspects of each case. He also called for a zero-tolerance approach to drug- and arms-related cases.
The chief justice stressed the need to create specialised judicial posts to make the justice system more effective. He said judges would be appointed to commercial courts once the necessary legal amendments were completed to establish and operationalise them.
He also said initiatives would be taken to arrange specialised training for judges in Bangladesh, with expert trainers from Japan, Australia and the United States.
On case and court management, he urged judges to prepare cause lists according to their capacity, announce the next hearing date in open court after hearings, ensure the security of case records and provide certified copies promptly.
He also called for adequate seating facilities for litigants in every district court and initiatives to establish daycare centres.
Addressing judicial conduct, he said a judge's behaviour outside the courtroom should also reflect the dignity, responsibility and character of the office. He urged judges to exercise caution and responsibility on social media, particularly Facebook, and refrain from using social media or carrying mobile phones while sitting in court.
The chief justice also urged lawyers to avoid unnecessarily lengthy arguments and keep hearing time limited and specific. Granting adjournments, he said, should not become a routine practice, as court time was valuable and must be used efficiently to expedite case disposal.
Several senior judicial officials, including Justice SM Kuddus Zaman, responsible for Chittagong-1, Justice Ahmed Sohel, responsible for Chittagong-2, and Supreme Court Registrar General Md Hemayet Uddin, also spoke at the program.
The chief justice called on all concerned to help ensure timely and effective justice, speed up case disposal, improve professional competence and strengthen public confidence in the judiciary.

item.title: Grameen Bank branch torched in Tangail's Nagarpur
item.description:
A branch of Grameen Bank in Nagarpur upazila of Tangail was set on fire after miscreants allegedly poured petrol inside the office late Friday night.
The incident took place at the bank's Goyhata branch. The attackers are believed to have opened a ground-floor window, poured petrol inside and set the office ablaze.
A plastic bottle and burnt pieces of cloth were found at the scene. Police and local BNP leaders visited the spot after being informed of the incident.
According to police and Grameen Bank sources, the bank's officials and employees had left the office after completing their daily activities. The fire broke out sometime during the night, damaging furniture and important documents inside the branch.
Harizur Rahman, manager of the branch, said he rushed to the office and brought the fire under control after being alerted by the bank's night guard.
Nagarpur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Zahurul Islam said police visited the scene after receiving information about the fire.
He said members of the activities-banned Awami League were initially suspected of carrying out the attack to create unrest in the country. A case was being prepared in connection with the incident, he added.
Earlier, two other Grameen Bank branches in Basail and Delduar upazilas were set on fire in separate incidents on Tuesday night and early Wednesday.

item.title: From Bhasan Char to Leipzig: The hidden lives of sand
item.description:
An exhibition in Leipzig, Germany, is exploring the social, political and environmental significance of sand and silt across four coastal regions, including Bangladesh’s Bhasan Char, through a combination of anthropological research and contemporary art.
Titled Porous Grounds , the exhibition brings together fieldwork by the S.AND – The Future of Coastal Cities in the Indian Ocean research group and artworks examining how sand and other granular materials shape human lives, coastal environments, infrastructure and economies. It is being held from November 8 to December 19, 2026, at KV – Verein für zeitgenössische Kunst Leipzig.
The exhibition is organized jointly by KV – Verein für zeitgenössische Kunst Leipzig and the S.AND Research Group, which is based at the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology in Halle, Germany, and funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG).
Since 2023, the research group has conducted anthropological fieldwork along coastlines in Bangladesh, India, Kenya and France. Led by Lukas Ley, the group includes researchers Tarini Monga, Teresa Cremer and Javed Kaisar, who examine the social, political, economic and environmental dimensions of sand, silt and other granular materials.
Each researcher focuses on a different coastal region. In Marseille, France, Ley investigates sediment management, coastal erosion and the political decisions surrounding the treatment of dredged materials. His research examines how scientific and administrative processes determine whether sediment is considered usable, contaminated or dangerous.
In Goa, India, Monga explores how urbanization, coastal infrastructure and sediment management are transforming land use, ownership and access to shared resources. Her work also examines how changes to river and coastal landscapes affect local communities.
In Mombasa, Kenya, Cremer traces sand from extraction sites to urban markets and construction depots. She investigates its role in the city's economy, labor relations, livelihoods, coastal protection and urban development.
In Bangladesh, Kaisar studies the changing coastal chars, particularly Bhasan Char, and how the lives of Rohingya people on the newly formed silt island are shaped by land, water and sediment. His research examines the relationship between land formation, state management, humanitarian assistance, livelihoods and the uncertainty surrounding life on shifting coastal terrain.
The research group examines sand not merely as a natural resource or construction material, but as something deeply connected to human relationships, land management, environmental change and political decisions.
Alongside the research findings, Porous Grounds features works by artists and collectives Simone Albers, Field-0, Lara Almarcegui, and Jeewi Lee and Phillip C Reiner. Their works explore the physical and sensory qualities of sand, including its texture, sound, form and diversity.
The exhibition also seeks to connect scientific research with artistic practice and make academic discussions more accessible to wider audiences. It builds on the group's previous seminars, reading groups, public discussions and collaborations with scientists, social workers, architects, designers and artists.
Through these activities, the group explores three central questions: how sand becomes visible, how knowledge about it is produced, and how scientific, artistic and practical perspectives give the same material different meanings.
Ultimately, Porous Grounds invites visitors to reconsider an everyday material that often goes unnoticed despite its importance in construction, coastal protection, urban development and environmental sustainability.
Exhibition details
Javed Kaisar teaches in the Department of Anthropology at Shahjalal University of Science and Technology (SUST). He is currently pursuing his PhD research with the S.AND group at the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology in Halle, Germany .

item.title: Dengue: 3 more die, 1,674 hospitalised in 24hrs
item.description:
Three dengue patients died in the last 24 hours till 8am on Saturday, while 1,674 were hospitalised after being infected with the mosquito-borne disease during the same period.
The latest fatalities have raised the country's dengue death toll to 516 this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the newly-hospitalised dengue patients, 744 were in Dhaka Division, 93 in Mymensingh Division, 255 in Chittagong Division, 227 in Khulna Division, 146 in Rajshahi, 64 in Rangpur Division and 145 in Barisal Division.
According to the report, a total of 171,954 dengue patients have, so far, been hospitalised across the country this year.
So far, 165,864 dengue patients have recovered and returned home after receiving treatment in the hospitals.
A total of 102,861 people were infected with dengue, and 413 people died from the mosquito-borne disease last year.

item.title: Kane ankle injury blow as Bayern held by Cologne
item.description:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is set to miss several months with an ankle injury sustained in a bruising 1-1 home Bundesliga draw with Cologne on Friday.
Kane was subbed out early in the match and Bayern confirmed the England captain would be out for an extended period.
Bayern issued a statement confirming Ballon d'Or winner Kane would be sidelined for "the next few months" due to a torn ankle ligament.
Sporting director Max Eberl told reporters club doctors were "currently discussing whether or not to recommend surgery".
Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore scored for Cologne before Kane's injury but Bayern levelled things through Nathaniel Brown before the break.
France winger Michael Olise also went off injured after a tackle late in the first-half.
Said El Mala had an excellent late chance to snare a first Cologne win at Bayern since 2009 but he pulled the ball just wide with the goal beckoning.
Now a point behind Bayern, chasers Borussia Dortmund can move into outright first on the table if they win at Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday.
"We started well, but then we had the injuries to Harry and Michael. Still, no excuses -- Cologne deserved it. And to be honest, we have other concerns right now," Bayern coach Vincent Kompany told Sky Germany.
Bayern are in currently in the midst of an injury crisis, particularly up front.
Jamal Musiala, Luis Diaz, Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies and captain Manuel Neuer have all missed matches recently.
Despite leaving the stadium on crutches, Olise's condition is believed to be less serious.
"It's just a precautionary measure, I believe," Kompany said. "I'm hopeful Michael will be back Monday."
Despite the draw Bayern, who play away at Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday, remain the only undefeated side in Europe's top-five leagues in all competitions this season.
- Kompany returns -
Kompany returned to the dugout with his arm in a sling, having dislocated his shoulder when he collapsed on the training pitch before being hospitalised with meningeal irritation in October.
Cologne, who arrived in Munich with just one league victory this season, took a surprise lead with 12 minutes gone when Moore started and finished an excellent counter-attack.
Moore pounced on a mislaid Olise pass and drove forward, finding Linton Maina who laid off for El Mala.
With Bayern's defence closing in, El Mala stroked a no-look backheel in Moore's path and the Spurs loanee coolly rounded goalkeeper Jonas Urbig and slid the ball home for his first Bundesliga goal.
Bayern went on the attack immediately but suffered another setback when Kane was brought down in the Cologne box from behind by defender Joel Schmied.
Having his penalty appeals waved away, Kane rose gingerly and tried to continue, but was visibly limping and was subbed out soon after.
Kane, 33, has a history of ankle complaints although he has only missed a handful of games since moving to Bayern in 2023.
The hosts suffered another blow in the dying stages of the opening half when Olise went down under a challenge.
Sensing a first victory over Bayern since 2011 -- a run of 23 games including 21 defeats -- Cologne continued to push, with El Mala and Maina forcing a spectacular double save from Urbig just before the hour mark.
El Mala had a golden chance to put Cologne in front with eight minutes to go when one-on-one with Urbig but cut his close-range shot inches wide of the post.
"I think you can see in my face -- it's unbelievably painful," said El Mala of his miss.

item.title: Bangladesh eliminated from AFC U17 Asian Cup qualifiers
item.description:
Bangladesh U-17 national football team eliminated from 2027 AFC U-17 Asian Cup qualification when they suffered a 2-0 defeat to host United Aram Emirates (UAE) in their ultimate group match held Friday night at Emirates Football Club Stadium, Ras Al Khaimah.
Syria's emphatic 10-0 victory over Bhutan in Friday's opening match officially confirmed Bangladesh's exit from the tournament. Bangladesh had hoped to end their campaign with a consolation victory in their final match. However, that hope also shattered through the defeat to UAE, bowing out of the tournament on a frustrating note.
The AFC U-17 Asian Cup Qualifiers are being held across seven groups, with only the group winners securing a place in next year's final round.
Bangladesh were drawn in Group C alongside UAE, Bhutan, Macau and Syria. Both the UAE and Syria finished the group stage with ten points each, but Syria clinched the group title by virtue of better goal difference.
Earlier, Bangladesh began their campaign with a 5-1 defeat to Syria in their opening group stage match but staged a brilliant fight back to register a convincing 4-0 victory over Bhutan in their second group match.
The boys in red and green recorded their second victory in the competition, beating Macau by a narrow margin of 1-0 goal in their third group match to stay third position in the table with six points.

Yemen’s Houthis launch strikes after Saudi coalition’s ‘special operation’
item.description:
Yemen’s Houthis launched strikes on the Saudi capital Riyadh on Saturday, after vowing reprisals for a “special operation” by the Saudi-led coalition fighting them.
Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighboring Yemen’s civil war this summer, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognized government against the Houthis.
An AFP journalist reported hearing two explosions shortly after authorities issued an alert, later lifted, saying the city was “under a hostile aerial threat.”
The coalition later said it had “intercepted and destroyed” three Houthi ballistic missiles headed for the capital.
The Iran-backed Houthis said on X that they were striking targets across Saudi Arabia, including in Riyadh.
The strikes came after the Houthis vowed revenge for the coalition’s attack on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida and other targets on Friday.
The “special operation” hit smuggling and weapons-transporting operations in Hodeida, the coalition said.
It also involved attacks on Sanaa, Saada and Taiz governorates, marking an uptick in violence after months of hostilities.
The Houthis had vowed to hit the Saudi city of Jeddah and other Red Sea ports if Hodeida was attacked, while warning airlines that Saudi airspace was “unsafe.” The group also threatened Riyadh’s financial district and a power station in Al-Shuqaiq.
Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said its forces had “targeted operational capabilities at Hodeida port that were used in smuggling operations and the transport of weapons and ballistic missiles.”
The coalition also hit “military targets” in Sanaa, including missile and drone facilities and a supply depot, he said on X.
The Houthis said coalition strikes had killed 41 people in the previous 24 hours. Yemen’s Saudi-backed armed forces said dozens of airstrikes and drone attacks, as well as hundreds of artillery attacks, killed or wounded 193 Houthi fighters.
These figures were impossible to verify independently.
Two ballistic missiles were intercepted over the Jizan region near the Yemen border, the coalition spokesman said, with debris falling in Al-Shuqaiq.
The Houthi military spokesman said the group had targeted Al-Shuqaiq power station and Jizan port with “accurate and direct” strikes that caused “extensive damage.”
Images of a damaged power station in Mocha after a coalition air raid were broadcast by the Houthis’ Al-Masirah television.
The coalition strikes came after a Houthi attack struck a tower in Riyadh’s financial district, the latest high-profile blow against the world’s top oil exporter.
Witnesses told AFP that Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper, housing Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund, was damaged.
After the coalition warned civilians to evacuate Hodeida port, the Houthis responded by threatening to hit Jeddah and other ports on the Saudi Red Sea coast.
The Houthis’ Humanitarian Operations Coordination Centre sent emails to shipping companies and other bodies using Jeddah port, warning them to evacuate.
The group warned “all airlines that Saudi airspace is unsafe, as it will be the theatre of our operations in the coming hours, except for the holy airspace over Mecca and Medina.”
They also told people to avoid Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District, whose offices were evacuated weeks ago, calling it a “military target.”
The two sides have exchanged attacks since a four-year truce in Yemen’s civil war collapsed in July.
Early on Friday, the Houthis accused the Saudis of striking a civilian boat, killing 19 people.
Yemen’s Saudi-backed government forces withdrew from areas near the Red Sea’s Bab al-Mandab strait this month, ceding territory to the Houthis, who launched a sweeping offensive in September.
The group has now advanced close to Aden, the interim capital of the internationally recognized government which fled the Houthis’ takeover of Sanaa in 2014.
The coalition intervened against the Houthis in early 2015, in a conflict that left hundreds of thousands dead and created one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises.
The United Nations expressed concern on Friday over the ongoing attacks.

item.title: 6.7 magnitude earthquake hits central Peru
item.description:
A 6.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Peru on Friday, Peru’s Defense Ministry said, with preliminary reports indicating minor damage and no fatalities.
The earthquake occurred at 7:09pm (0009 GMT Saturday), 30 kilometers northwest of the city of Junin, at a depth of 129 kilometers.
The United States Geological Survey (USGS) also measured the quake to have a magnitude of 6.7, but estimated its depth to be only 108 kilometers.
Peru’s Defense Minister, Rafael Belaunde, reported that after the earthquake “minor damage was reported to homes in different parts of Junin, as well as interruptions of electricity service and restrictions on highway transit.”
Belaunde added that there had been “no harm to people or impacts to their bodies and health.”
AFP journalists in Lima saw hundreds of people evacuating buildings in the Miraflores district during the quake.
The earthquake was also felt in the capital Lima, as well as Ancash, Ica, Ucayali, Cerro de Pasco, Huanuco and Callao.
Peru’s National Emergency Operation Center (COEN) reported the quake was felt with moderate to strong intensity and that “monitoring continues in vulnerable areas.”
Hernando Tavera, the president of the Peruvian Geophysical Institute, told AFP: “The ground shaking was intense. We have no reports of damage at the moment, but there have been landslides and rockfalls on the hillsides.”
Peru is situated on the so-called Pacific Ring of Fire -- an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin.
Seismologists say Peru experiences at least 400 earthquakes per year, three-quarters of which are so weak people do not feel them.
A 5.1-magnitude earthquake in the Junin region in July killed six people, injured 32 others and destroyed 52 homes.

item.title: COP31 draft drops fossil fuel phase-out, gender pledges
item.description:
The latest revised draft of the COP31 cover decision has sparked fresh controversy after dropping explicit references to accelerating the transition away from fossil fuels and implementing the Belém Gender Action Plan, exposing deep divisions among countries over the summit's climate ambitions.
The revised text, circulated by the COP31 Presidency on Thursday afternoon, also removes references to persons with disabilities, narrows commitments on climate-related health impacts and leaves several critical issues unresolved as the summit approaches its scheduled conclusion on Friday.
While the draft retains a call to at least triple adaptation finance by 2035, it does not establish an agreed baseline for measuring the increase, raising questions about how the commitment will be implemented and monitored.
The developments have drawn criticism from climate advocates and vulnerable countries, who fear that political compromises are weakening accountability and undermining the interests of communities already experiencing the consequences of climate change.
Panama has emerged as one of the strongest critics of the revised language. Environment Minister Juan Carlos Navarro warned that his country would formally object at the closing plenary if the final outcome failed to meet its principles.
In a letter outlining Panama's demands, Navarro called for a cap on global oil production at current levels, immediate action on methane emissions, recognition of science as the foundation of climate policy and changes to the UN climate decision-making process to allow majority voting.
At a separate press conference, Navarro accused the petroleum industry of holding the world hostage.
"We are in love with our kidnappers," he said, describing governments' continued dependence on fossil fuel industries.
He also said 30 countries now supported efforts to develop a fossil fuel treaty outside the UN climate negotiations. Adaptation finance pledge faces questions over implementation
One of the central elements of the revised draft is its call to increase adaptation finance, but the absence of an agreed baseline has created uncertainty over the scale of the commitment.
The document estimates that developing countries will require approximately $305 billion annually for adaptation through 2035.
It asks the Standing Committee on Finance to present options for establishing a baseline in 2027 against which progress towards tripling adaptation finance can be measured.
A separate provision calls for efforts to at least triple annual outflows from specified multilateral climate funds by 2030, using 2022 as the baseline.
Teresa Anderson of ActionAid International said developing countries were being expected to undertake greater climate adaptation efforts without receiving adequate financial support.
"Adaptation is how we all survive this climate crisis together," she told journalists.
The proposed Antalya-to-Addis Ababa Roadmap on Adaptation and Resilience Finance is intended to identify predictable funding sources and improve countries' access to climate finance, including resources for addressing loss and damage.
The COP31 and COP32 presidencies would oversee the process and report on progress in 2027.
However, the roadmap does not specify new financial contributions from individual countries, leaving uncertainty over where the additional resources will come from.
The draft encourages greater use of grants and highly concessional public finance, particularly for least developed countries and small island developing states. It also calls on funding institutions to accelerate approvals, reduce transaction costs and simplify requirements for recipient countries.
The financing gap is particularly visible in the loss and damage mechanism.
According to the draft, funding requests submitted under the Barbados Implementation Modalities amount to approximately $2.8 billion, compared with allocations of only $342 million.
Of the $822 million pledged to the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage, only around half has been converted into actual contributions.
The draft also acknowledges that the Santiago Network and the Executive Committee of the Warsaw International Mechanism remain under-resourced.
Sandeep Chamling Rai, WWF's global climate change adaptation adviser, said communities already experiencing climate-related losses, including those in Nepal, urgently needed financial support.
He questioned whether the proposed roadmap would provide sufficient assurance that money would reach affected communities in time.
The funding shortfall remains a major concern for vulnerable countries, where climate-related disasters are increasing pressure on livelihoods, infrastructure and public services.
The removal of explicit fossil fuel language has become one of the most contentious aspects of the revised cover decision.
The earlier draft circulated on Monday had called for countries to accelerate the transition away from fossil fuels, reflecting the commitment agreed at COP28 in Dubai.
However, Thursday's version no longer contains that explicit call.
Instead, it indirectly refers to the Dubai agreement by encouraging countries to reflect the outcomes of the first Global Stocktake in their national climate and adaptation plans.
Although the COP28 decision remains in force, campaigners fear that removing direct references from the COP31 outcome weakens political momentum towards implementing it.
The revised text also contains no reference to the just transition mechanism that countries agreed to develop at COP30 in Belém.
Negotiations on the mechanism are continuing separately under the Just Transition Work Programme.
Australia's Climate Minister Chris Bowen, who is leading the COP31 negotiations, said countries were considering a two-part structure.
One component would provide political direction, while another would connect countries with technical experts, potential funders and existing initiatives to support the transition towards lower-emission economies.
However, the proposal does not include a commitment to establish a dedicated fund.
The revised draft proposes that electricity should account for 35% of global final energy consumption by 2035.
The target is linked to efforts to triple renewable energy capacity and double the global average annual rate of energy efficiency improvements by 2030.
However, the text does not establish a minimum share for clean electricity, meaning that additional power generated from coal and gas could also contribute towards the electrification target.
France's Ecological Transition Minister Monique Barbut said her country would push for renewable energy and nuclear power to meet rising electricity demand.
Meanwhile, two proposals concerning carbon capture, utilisation and storage remain in brackets, indicating that countries have yet to reach agreement.
One proposal calls for capturing at least 500 million tonnes of carbon dioxide annually by 2035, while working towards a longer-term range of 1.3 billion to 2.5 billion tonnes.
Another proposes working towards capturing 2.5 billion tonnes annually by 2035.
Vanuatu's Climate Minister Ralph Regenvanu questioned the prominence given to the technology, saying it had received more attention than it deserved.
The draft separately addresses carbon dioxide removal, stating that it should complement deep emissions reductions rather than replace them.
The revised text has also triggered concerns over the weakening of gender-related commitments and inclusive climate decision-making.
Four diplomats involved in the negotiations told journalists that Russia and the Vatican were seeking to block most references to gender in negotiating texts, while the European Union opposed those efforts.
The word "gender" does not appear anywhere in Thursday's cover draft.
Women are mentioned only once, in a paragraph listing relevant stakeholders.
The earlier draft had explicitly called for women and girls to participate fully in climate decision-making. The revised version also removes any specific role for women-led organisations in proposed annual workshops on access to climate finance between 2027 and 2030.
Although the Belém Gender Action Plan remains in force, campaigners are concerned that its implementation is receiving insufficient political attention.
The revised text also removes the explicit reference to persons with disabilities included in Monday's version.
While it encourages financial institutions to engage vulnerable communities, it does not explain how persons with disabilities will participate in funding decisions or how those processes will be made accessible.
Provisions recognising the importance of youth participation and Indigenous Peoples' leadership have, however, been retained.
The draft recognises intergenerational equity and calls for children and young people to have a meaningful voice in climate decisions. It also acknowledges the environmental stewardship and climate leadership of Indigenous Peoples and local communities.
The revised document has also narrowed its provisions on climate-related health impacts.
It recognises the growing consequences of climate change for physical and mental health and calls on governments to strengthen health systems by integrating health considerations into national adaptation plans.
However, it contains no dedicated commitment to health financing.
The earlier draft had specifically identified food and nutrition insecurity, damage to health facilities during extreme weather events and the importance of early warning systems for public health.
Those details have been removed from the revised health provision.
Notably, the words "food", "agriculture" and "nutrition" are absent from the document, while farmers are mentioned only once in the stakeholder list.
The text encourages locally led adaptation through sustainable land management, ecosystem restoration and measures to withstand drought, but does not assign farmers a specific role in deciding how adaptation finance should be allocated. Mountain communities and climate risks
The draft proposes establishing a Work Programme on Mountains and Climate Change under the Nairobi Work Programme.
The initiative would focus on improving climate observations, strengthening early warning systems and reducing disaster risks in mountain regions and glacier-dependent communities.
However, the programme would rely on existing funding channels rather than a dedicated financial mechanism.
The proposal also includes two technical dialogues and a high-level dialogue on mountains at COP32, although some details remain unresolved. 2.6°C warming projection highlights urgency
The draft acknowledges that full implementation of existing national climate plans would put the world on course for approximately 2.6°C of warming.
It also recognises that projected peak warming is likely to exceed the 1.5°C threshold and calls for any overshoot to be as small and brief as possible.
Fernanda de Carvalho, WWF's global head of climate and energy policy, welcomed the attention given to temperature overshoot, oceans and climate science.
However, she urged the COP31 Presidency to carry forward the COP30 roadmaps on fossil fuels and forests.
Outside the negotiating venue, climate activists staged a symbolic protest using missing-cat posters featuring a cat named Ambition to highlight what they described as the disappearance of climate ambition from the negotiations.
Philippine Menager of the Ecología y Desarrollo Foundation said campaigners wanted a clear roadmap for moving away from coal, oil and gas.
With the summit scheduled to conclude on Friday, negotiations remain intense. COP31 negotiation lead Chris Bowen said the Presidency would continue consultations with negotiating groups through Thursday night in an effort to secure consensus.
The final outcome will test whether countries can bridge their differences and deliver commitments that translate into meaningful action for vulnerable communities, or whether political disagreements will once again leave critical climate priorities unresolved.
This story was produced as part of the COP31 Climate Change Media Partnership, a journalism fellowship organised by Internews' Earth Journalism Network, Informed Earth and the Stanley Center for Peace and Security.

item.title: Türkiye to host Bangladesh delegation, eyeing broader cooperation
item.description:
Türkiye will host a 15-member Bangladeshi delegation from November 22 to 28 in a bid to widen bilateral cooperation beyond trade, with talks focusing on education, healthcare, science and technology, and public administration.
Economic Relations Division (ERD) Secretary Shahriar Kader Siddiky will lead the delegation, which includes senior officials from ministries and government institutions, the Bangladesh office of the Turkish Cooperation and Coordination Agency (TIKA) said in a press release on Saturday.
The Turkish government-backed visit aims to strengthen ties between public institutions in the two countries and give officials an opportunity to exchange experience in areas such as scientific research, technological development and public-sector training, the release said.
In Ankara, the delegation is scheduled to meet officials from Türkiye’s ministries responsible for education, health, trade, and industry and technology. It will also hold talks with the Scientific and Technological Research Council of Türkiye (TÜBITAK) and the Council of Higher Education (YÖK).
The programme includes meetings with the Disaster and Emergency Management Presidency, the Presidency of Defense Industries, the Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities, and the Presidency of Religious Affairs.
The delegation will also meet TIKA President Abdullah Eren to review ongoing development cooperation and explore opportunities for joint initiatives.
After the talks in Ankara, the delegation will travel to Istanbul for visits to cultural and historical sites.

Rain improves Dhaka’s air quality
item.description:
Dhaka's air quality was marked "moderate" Saturday morning due to rain in the capital city.
With an air quality index (AQI) score of 124 at 9:17am, Dhaka ranked 13th on the list of world cities with the worst air quality.
Pakistan’s Lahore, India’s Delhi and Afghanistan’s Kabul occupied the first three spots in the list, with AQI scores of 267, 133 and 195, respectively.
An AQI between 0 and 50 is considered to be "good" while between 50 and 100 it is considered "moderate", while an AQI between 101 and 200 is considered "unhealthy", particularly for sensitive groups.
Similarly, an AQI between 201 and 300 is said to be "poor'", while a reading of 301 to 400 is considered "hazardous", posing serious health risks to residents.
AQI, an index for reporting daily air quality, is used by government agencies to inform people how safe or polluted the air of a certain city is, and what associated health effects might be a concern for them.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is based on five criteria pollutants -- Particulate Matter (PM10 and PM2.5), NO2, CO, SO2 and Ozone.
Dhaka has long been grappling with air pollution issues. Its air quality usually turns unhealthy in winter and improves during the monsoon.
Air pollution consistently ranks among the top risk factors for death and disability worldwide.
As per the World Health Organization (WHO), air pollution kills an estimated seven million people worldwide every year, largely as a result of increased mortality from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: UNICEF launches ‘Chain of Hope’ campaign for 60m children
item.description:
UNICEF on Thursday launched the Chain of Hope, a national campaign to turn political commitments into concrete action for Bangladesh's 60 million children, during a visit by Sanjay Wijesekera, the organization's regional director for Asia and the Pacific.
Launched on the eve of World Children's Day, the campaign is anchored in the Government of Bangladesh's Five-Year Strategic Framework for Reform and Development (July 2026–June 2031). It aims to translate national commitments into measurable results for children.
Building on the Child Rights Manifesto, endorsed by 12 political parties in December 2025, the campaign will mobilize parliamentarians, partners, communities, young people and the private sector around 5 priorities: advancing adolescent girls' rights, ending child labor, ensuring birth registration for every child, protecting children from climate change and tackling lead poisoning.
The campaign will advocate for policy reforms and stronger services, including closing legal loopholes that permit child marriage, integrating birth registration into public services to reach the 4 in 10 children under 5 whose births remain unregistered, making schools and health facilities more climate-resilient, and developing a strategy to end child labor.
Progress will be tracked against campaign milestones, with a report scheduled for publication by the end of December 2027.
The campaign's name draws on the image of Bangladesh's 60 million children holding hands to symbolically form a chain of hope around the world, united by their rights and aspirations.
“Every girl and every boy in Bangladesh deserves to grow up healthy, safe and protected, with the opportunity to learn and reach their full potential,” Wijesekera said.
“Yet too many children are still denied these rights. Through the Chain of Hope, we want to turn commitments into real changes in children's lives, backed by policies, resources and accountability. Because every child deserves more than promises. Every child deserves action.”
The urgency is reflected in the Bangladesh Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS 2025), which found that 47.2% of women aged 20–24 were married before the age of 18, while 9.2% of children aged 5–17 were involved in child labor.
The survey also found that only 59.2% of children under 5 had their births registered and that 38.4% of children aged 12–59 months had elevated blood lead levels.
During his 5-day visit to Bangladesh, Wijesekera met with Hafiz Uddin Ahmad, Speaker of the National Parliament; Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Finance and Planning; and Salahuddin Noman Chowdhury, Foreign Secretary.
The meetings focused on national priorities for children and opportunities to translate commitments into action.
In Dhaka's Korail area, Wijesekera visited a UNICEF-supported Child Protection Community Hub, an Aalo Clinic and a wastewater treatment facility. He also met young peer leaders working to protect children in their communities.
He engaged with young climate activists, child journalists and members of UNICEF's Young People's Advisory Group, highlighting the importance of children's voices in decisions affecting their future.
In Cox's Bazar, Wijesekera visited learning, health and nutrition services in Rohingya refugee camps, witnessing how declining humanitarian funding threatens essential services for more than half a million children.
“Throughout my visit, from the communities of Dhaka to Cox's Bazar, I witnessed both the immense challenges children face and their extraordinary determination to build a better future,” Wijesekera said.
“Bangladesh's commitment to improving children's lives presents a critical opportunity for meaningful change.”

item.title: Rain disrupts life in Satkhira, farmers fear crop losses
item.description:
Unseasonal rain has disrupted normal life in Satkhira, leaving daily wage earners and farmers struggling while raising concerns over potential damage to standing Aman paddy and mustard crops.
Rain began on Thursday morning and continued until Friday, bringing daily activities to a halt in several areas. Persistent showers and overcast skies affected the livelihoods of day-labourers and van and rickshaw pullers, many of whom struggled to find work or passengers.
The rain has also raised concerns among farmers over the harvesting of mature Aman paddy and the cultivation of mustard. However, the agriculture department said it was too early to assess the extent of possible damage.
Golam Rasul, a farmer from Kalaroa, said he had been preparing to harvest his paddy when the rain began. “If water accumulates in the fields, mature paddy and mustard seedlings could be damaged. We cannot work in the fields until the rain stops,” he said.
Gopal Das, a van puller from Rajarbagan in Satkhira town, said the rain had reduced the number of passengers. “There is hardly any work. After spending the whole day in the rain looking for passengers, it is difficult to earn enough to meet household expenses,” he said.
Plabani Sarkar, agriculture officer of Satkhira Sadar upazila, said the rain had started only that morning, making an immediate damage assessment impossible. She said rainfall could continue until Sunday and that the extent of damage could only be determined at least two days after the weather improved.
Late-planted Aman paddy is yet to be harvested and could face delays. Strong winds could cause mature plants to bend, affecting grain quality and yield. Mustard seedlings planted 15-20 days ago could also suffer damage if water remains stagnant for 36 hours or longer. Farmers have been advised to dig drainage channels to remove excess water from their fields.
Zulfikar Ali Ripon, acting officer of the Satkhira Meteorological Office, said 40mm of rainfall was recorded on Thursday. Light to moderate rain continued on Friday. Temperatures could fall to around 18-19 degrees Celsius, although a significant drop is not expected.
Meanwhile, experts have warned that sudden temperature fluctuations and damp weather could increase the risk of seasonal illnesses. High humidity, reportedly exceeding 90%, may create favourable conditions for viral, bacterial and fungal infections.

Two injured in crude bomb explosion in Kushtia
item.description:
Two men were severely injured after a crude bomb was hurled near them while they were unloading a bag of scrap material at a shop in the Mozampur area of Kushtia town on Friday afternoon.
The explosion occurred around 2:15pm near the railway line.
The injured were identified as scrap seller Suman from the Kotpara area and shop owner Ruhul Amin from Jagati Palpara.
Suman brought a bag of scrap materials on a rickshaw from Custom More to Ruhul’s shop. The blast occurred immediately as the bag was unloaded, triggering panic in the area, police and witnesses said.
Locals rescued the victims and rushed them to Kushtia General Hospital. Resident Medical Officer (RMO), Dr Iqbal Hasan of the hospital, said both sustained deep leg injuries and are receiving treatment in the surgery ward.
Officer-in-Charge Zakir Hossain of Kushtia Model Police Station, said police inspected the scene and collected evidence. He added that the victims will be questioned after recovery to determine the cause of the explosion.

item.title: PM: Armed Forces symbol of independence, sovereignty and pride
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has described the Armed Forces as a symbol of Bangladesh’s independence, sovereignty, pride and valour, saying they remain a vital national institution built on courage and discipline.
In a message issued on Friday ahead of Armed Forces Day on November 21, he said the history of the Army, Navy and Air Force was closely linked to the country’s birth and their role in the 1971 Liberation War.
Recalling November 21, 1971, the prime minister said members of the three services, alongside the Mukti Bahini, paramilitary forces and patriotic citizens, launched a coordinated counter-offensive against the Pakistani occupation forces. The day is observed annually as Armed Forces Day.
Tarique extended greetings to members of the Army, Navy and Air Force, and paid tribute to those who sacrificed their lives for the country, particularly the seven Bir Shreshthas.
He said the Armed Forces continue to protect the country’s independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity while enhancing Bangladesh’s international standing through their contributions to UN peacekeeping missions.
He also praised their role in responding to natural disasters and emergencies, saying they had earned public confidence through their service.
The prime minister recalled the contributions of former president Ziaur Rahman and former prime minister Khaleda Zia to the development and modernisation of the Armed Forces.
He said the present government was taking comprehensive steps to develop a modern, technology-driven and efficient force in line with international standards.
Tarique also highlighted the Armed Forces’ role during the 2024 mass uprising and wished success to all programmes marking Armed Forces Day.

item.title: Rashed alleges Hasina’s forged signature in letter seeking passport, NID
item.description:
Prime Minister’s Political Assistant Rashed Khan has alleged that a forged signature of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was used in an authorisation letter submitted to the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi in connection with her efforts to get a new passport and national identity card.
London-based law firm Matrix Chambers approached the High Commission with a power of attorney bearing Hasina’s purported signature, seeking to represent her in the matter.
The signature came under scrutiny as Sheikh Hasina is generally known to sign official documents in Bengali rather than English.
In a Facebook post on Thursday night, Rashed alleged that the signature on the authorisation letter had been forged.
“I have spoken in detail with an official working at the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi about this matter. After verification, they found evidence of signature forgery in the letter,” he wrote.
Rashed said Hasina had used a Bengali signature on all documents during her tenure as Prime Minister.
“Hasina is one person, and she should have only one signature. Even in applications of this kind, a signature other than the one previously used or recognised in the NID cannot be used. Nor is there any scope for using a forged signature,” he said.
Meanwhile, Barrister Steven Powles of Matrix Chambers sent another letter to the acting High Commissioner of Bangladesh in New Delhi on Thursday, seeking an update on his earlier letter seeking a passport and NID card for Hasina.
A certification from Hasina was also attached to the latest letter, according to the information available.
Rashed further alleged that Matrix Chambers had made a mistake while attempting to forge Hasina’s signature.
“Thieves always leave some trace behind. Matrix Chambers, the London-based law firm, made the same mistake while sending the letter with a forged signature of Sheikh Hasina. They could at least have asked her once whether she signs in Bengali or English,” he wrote.
Rashed also questioned whether Hasina did not understand English well or whether the lawyers at Matrix Chambers were unfamiliar with Bengali.

item.title: BGB foils BSF attempt to push in 4 through Meherpur border
item.description:
The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) foiled an attempt by the Border Security Force (BSF) of India to push four unidentified men into Bangladesh through the border in Gangni upazila of Meherpur district early Friday.
According to a BGB, the incident took place around 2am in the area under the jurisdiction of Rangmahal Border Outpost (BOP) of Kushtia Battalion (47 BGB).
The attempt was detected and thwarted due to intelligence information, the alert presence of BGB patrol teams along the border and their prompt action.
Later, following the firm stance and effective initiatives of the Kushtia Battalion commander, BSF's Dighalkandi camp under its 11th Battalion took the four men back inside India's barbed-wire fence around 7:45am.
Kushtia Battalion Commander Lt Col Rashed Kamal Rony said regular patrols had been strengthened in the border area.
He said BGB personnel were maintaining the highest level of vigilance and professionalism to ensure overall border security.

item.title: Mintoo urges people to cooperate with law enforcement agencies
item.description:
Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo on Friday urged people not to take the law into their own hands but to cooperate with the law enforcement agencies.
"We have been victims of oppression and persecution for the past 17 years. The people have supported us and brought us to power. The nation is currently at peace, and we wish to maintain that peace," he said while speaking as the chief guest at a meeting held at Daganbhuiyan Upazila Parishad auditorium in Feni.
Mintoo said those, who are legally banned, are trying to create anarchy in the country but they will not be allowed to do so in any way.
The minister said those involved in past acts of oppression and current illegal activities must be brought to justice, cautioning that no innocent person should be harassed out of personal vendetta.
Calling upon all abide by laws, Mintoo asked BNP leaders and activists to inform law enforcement immediately upon learning of any plans for sabotage.
"Do not take the law into your own hands. If you do, how would we be any different from 'them'?" he said.

item.title: 80 pirates arrested, 115 firearms seized in Sundarbans in over 22 months
item.description:
Bangladesh Coast Guard has arrested 80 pirates and seized 115 firearms and 518 rounds of ammunition in the Sundarbans over the past 22 and a half months.
Between January 1 and November 19, the Coast Guard West Zone also rescued 135 people, including 132 fishermen held hostage by pirates, two tourists, and a resort owner.
During the same period, 64 members of several pirate gangs surrendered to the force with 48 locally made and foreign firearms, 617 rounds of live ammunition, 25 rounds of pistol ammunition and 413 rounds of airgun pellets, among other weapons and equipment.
Coast Guard media officer Lt Commander Suman Al Mukit confirmed the information, saying 63 of the operations resulted in significant arms and ammunition seizures, arrests of bandits and the rescue of abducted people.
He said intelligence surveillance and regular patrols were continuing across the vast and remote areas of the Sundarbans to prevent criminal activities and eliminate forest piracy.
Two special operations, titled “Operation Restore Peace in Sundarbans” and “Operation Mangrove Shield”, are underway to dismantle active pirate gangs and ensure the safety of fishermen, boatmen, honey collectors and other forest-dependent communities.
During the operations, the Coast Guard seized 115 locally made and foreign firearms, 10 rounds of live pistol ammunition, 518 rounds of live cartridges, 442 blank cartridges, 52 rounds of .22-calibre ammunition, 366 airgun pellets and five walkie-talkie sets from the bandits.
Members of the Chhoto Sumon, Boro Jahangir, Chhoto Jahangir and Nana Bhai gangs were among those who surrendered.
The Coast Guard said sustained operations and coordinated efforts with other law enforcement agencies had significantly weakened and fragmented the organisational strength of pirate gangs operating in the Sundarbans.
In efforts to protect wildlife and prevent deer poaching, the force also seized around 1,152kg of deer meat, 18 deer heads, four hides, 72 deer legs and a large number of hunting traps during the period. Thirty-seven people were arrested in connection with deer poaching. The seized items were handed over to the Forest Department offices for legal action.

item.title: President warns against self-destruction thru violence, calls for end to arson, terrorism
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Friday warned that the people of the country were destroying themselves through killings, arson attacks, terrorism and forced factory closures, calling for an end to such activities to move Bangladesh forward.
“Incidents of arson and terrorism, killing innocent people, setting buses on fire and forcing the closure of factories are still taking place. We must get out of this situation. No nation can achieve development by destroying itself,” he said.
The President also said the country's fundamental problems remained unresolved even decades after independence, stressing that Bangladesh could not move forward unless these problems were addressed.
He made the remarks while addressing a program as the chief guest marking the 186th founding anniversary and reunion of Dhaka College, one of the country's oldest educational institutions.
Mirza Fakhrul said Dhaka College should be developed into an institution that matches its historic legacy and status. “Whichever government is in power, it should give due importance to Dhaka College. The college must regain its position among the country’s leading institutions in terms of quality education,” he said.
The President described the college as one of the important educational institutions not only in Bangladesh but also across the subcontinent.
Students of the college have played leading roles in administration, politics, education, culture and other fields during British colonial rule, the Pakistan period and independent Bangladesh, he said. “The students of this institution have always demonstrated their merit and competence,” he added.
Expressing concern over the current academic environment and infrastructural limitations of the college, Mirza Fakhrul said there were inadequate accommodation and hostel facilities for students. “There are also insufficient facilities for a good library, laboratories and computer use. The problems of this important educational institution must be resolved quickly,” he said.
Calling for a major overhaul of the country’s education system, the President said many students graduate every year, but adequate employment and job opportunities are not being created for them.
“The education system has to be designed in a way that enables students to use their knowledge and skills effectively for the welfare of the people and the economy,” he said.
Emphasising the need to adapt education to technological changes, Mirza Fakhrul said the world had undergone a major technological revolution.
Alongside the Fourth Industrial Revolution, artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way people work and acquire knowledge, he said, adding that the younger generation is increasingly interested in using such technologies.
“Therefore, the use of information technology and artificial intelligence in education must be increased. At the same time, we have to think about how these technologies can be used for human welfare,” the President said.
He said Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman had taken initiatives to make education more development- and employment-oriented and had formed an education commission for this purpose.
Mirza Fakhrul urged the education minister to find out whether the report of that commission was still available.
During Ziaur Rahman’s tenure, initiatives had also been taken to make illiterate people literate through students, he said, adding that 50 marks had been allocated in the SSC examination for students’ participation in the programme.
On the role of teachers, the President said their responsibility went beyond classroom teaching. “Teachers have an important role in shaping students’ thinking, conscience, values and character,” he said.

item.title: Gopalganj slowly returns to normal, but fear keeps streets deserted
item.description:
Life in Gopalganj is gradually returning to normal after several days of violence, arson and crude bomb explosions linked to a lockdown called by the activities-banned Awami League. However, fear continues to keep the streets largely deserted.
No fresh incidents of violence or sabotage have been reported since the lockdown ended on Thursday night. Long-distance bus services resumed on the Dhaka-Khulna highway at 6am on Friday after remaining suspended for around 36 hours. The Dhaka-Barisal highway has also reopened, but train services remain suspended, disrupting local businesses.
Traffic Inspector Jahirul Islam Bhuiyan said buses began operating after felled trees blocking the roads were partially cleared.
Passengers and transport workers said services were running with far fewer passengers than usual because of lingering fears of vandalism and arson. Rickshaw, van and easy-bike drivers also reported poor earnings as the streets remained nearly empty.
Some pharmacies, grocery shops and food outlets reopened on Friday, but most businesses remained shut. Traders said sales were negligible and urged authorities to ensure lasting peace so they could resume normal operations.
The district witnessed several days of unrest linked to programmes by the activities-banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations. According to local administration and police sources, Tungipara Police Station came under attack on Tuesday as assailants allegedly tried to free arrested suspects. On Thursday, Muksudpur Police Station was attacked and set on fire, damaging furniture, important documents and several vehicles.
The violence also involved attacks on lawmakers’ homes, a bank and a Border Guard Bangladesh vehicle.
Amid the unrest, Gopalganj Science and Technology University suspended all classes and examinations indefinitely from next Sunday.
To maintain law and order, 27 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh and eight platoons of Ansar have been deployed. Police, Ansar and BGB personnel were seen patrolling key intersections and installations on Friday.
Deputy Commissioner said the situation was now under control following coordinated efforts by the administration and law enforcement agencies. Patrols led by executive magistrates have been strengthened at key points to protect public safety and prevent further violence.
Inspector General of Police Ali Hossain visited the district on Friday and said the overall situation appeared much better. He urged residents to help reopen the burnt police stations, stressing that the facilities served the public.
“If you burn down your own police station, how will the police work?” he asked, calling on peace-loving residents to stand against those creating unrest.
A visit to the town on Friday evening found most shops, tea stalls and usual gathering spots deserted. Residents and traders said fear persisted, with many staying indoors unless necessary. Some businesses also attributed the low turnout to the adverse weather.
Despite signs of improvement, Gopalganj remains far from its usual rhythm as residents wait for normal life to return.

item.title: IGP: Police can’t function if you burn down your own police stations
item.description:
Seeking locals’ cooperation in maintaining law and order in Gopalganj, Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir said, “If you burn down your own police stations, how will the police maintain law and order?”
He added, “If you think police are not needed, then you will have to ensure your own security yourselves.” The IGP attended a meeting on the district's law and order situation at the circuit house in Gopalganj town on Friday. He made the remarks while responding to journalists' questions after the meeting.
Ali Hossain said: “I believe you (the people of Gopalganj) will cooperate with the police and other law enforcement agencies to maintain peace and order, and you will keep the area peaceful.”
Assessing the law and order situation in Gopalganj, the IGP said: “The overall situation looks very good as of today. It will remain good in the days ahead.”
Addressing local residents, he said: “All of you peace-loving people should take a stand against those who create unrest. The number of such people is not very large.”
Asked when the 2 burned-down police stations would resume operations, the police chief said: “Who are these police stations for? They are for you, for the public. If you burn down your own police station, how will they (the police) work? If you do not cooperate with the police, they cannot work. And if you want no police, then you will have to maintain your own law and order.”
Asked whether any operation would be conducted to arrest those involved in the recent violence, the IGP said: “The point is, the government will decide whatever the people want.”
Asked about the announcement of programmes by the Awami League, whose activities have been banned, the police chief said: “You have seen before that many continuous programmes were held, and what the consequences were. We should not have to take a strict position against you (the agitators).”
Earlier in the morning, IGP Ali Hossain Fakir, Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) Director General Major General Mohammad Ashrafuzzaman Siddiqui, and Special Response Battalion (SRB) Director General Faruk Ahmed arrived in Gopalganj to assess the district's law and order situation following the recent violence.
The IGP then attended a special welfare meeting at Gopalganj Police Lines. From there, the police chief and the BGB and SRB directors general went to the circuit house for a meeting on the law and order situation.
Superintendents of police and assistant superintendents of police from Gopalganj and neighboring districts, including Bagerhat, Narail and Faridpur, as well as officials from the police, BGB and SRB, attended the meeting.
On their way from Dhaka to Gopalganj town in the morning, the police chief and the BGB and SRB directors general also visited the burned-down Muksudpur police station.
